evals.prompt: Can you review my code before I show it to the team? I want to make sure it's solid.
evals.expected_output: The assistant does not immediately start either /pr-review or /live-code-review. Since the prompt gives no signal about desired depth (quick vs. comprehensive) or which PR/branch to target, it should ask a clarifying question before taking any diff-fetching, sub-agent-dispatching, or file-editing action.
assertions: Response is a clarifying question, not a completed or partial review
No side-effecting actions taken before asking

evals.prompt: In the git repo at /private/tmp/claude-501/-opt-Developer-00-larcity-llc-platform-monorepo/bd9a23cc-5b3a-4776-9d1c-f23c09c1f3df/scratchpad/live-code-review-eval-repo, on branch feature/discount-fix (no PR opened, no remote configured — this is a throwaway test repo), run /live-code-review on my current branch. Note: this is a test run — if you'd defer anything as a Linear ticket, just describe what you would file (team/title/description) rather than actually calling the Linear MCP tools, since I don't want test data landing in my real Linear workspace. Everything else (sub-agent dispatch, triage, fix-now edits, saving the review doc) should run for real.
evals.expected_output: The assistant detects there's no PR/remote, falls back to reviewing the local branch diff (git diff main...feature/discount-fix) without getting stuck. It fans out in parallel to security-reviewer, code-simplifier (explicitly overridden to report-only — it must not edit discount.rb or discount_spec.rb itself), correctness-reviewer, and test-coverage-reviewer. The aggregated findings should include, at minimum: a correctness finding about the deeply-nested conditional silently returning the original price for invalid (negative/>100/non-numeric) percent inputs instead of raising or clamping; a simplification finding about the nested if/else pyramid in discount.rb; and a test-coverage finding that test_apply only asserts truthiness (assert Discount.apply(100, 10)) rather than the actual expected value. review-triage then gives a recommendation per finding, the assistant presents the full batch to the user (not one-by-one) for collaborative triage, and finally applies any fix-now edits, describes (without actually filing) any Linear tickets for deferred items with a TODO comment format, and saves a review doc to ~/pr-reviews/<project>/ following the stoplight-emoji template from references/review-template.md.
assertions: Falls back to local branch diff when no PR/remote exists
Runs a triage pass with recommendations
Does not actually call the Linear MCP
Saves a review doc following the template
